meshFindings.suspect: normal-packing: does the engine decode vertex normals the same way mesh_rw.py packs them?

findings.claim: The engine never CPU-decodes vertex normals. It builds a D3D9 vertex declaration and lets the GPU decode the packed-normal dword. So the 'decode' the tooling must match is the D3DDECLTYPE the engine assigns to the normal element, not a bit-unpack in code.
findings.engineEvidence: hero_mesh_decomp.txt: none of the 96 functions contain a normal bit-unpack (all 'Normal' string hits are shop-list/'Normalised time' UI, not geometry). The normal path lives in CVertexShaderInput{Static,Animated}::Initialise (0x00a90560/0x00a90630, decomp_mesh_geo8.c:44-148) which append declaration elements via FUN_00ab3810(usage,typeCode), and CVertexShaderInput::GenerateD3DDeclaration (0x00ab3870, decomp_mesh_geo10.c:44-165) which maps each internal typeCode through DAT_0129e9cc[typeCode] to a real D3DDECLTYPE byte (written at :120 CONCAT12(5,(byte)iVar7)) and accumulates the stride via the type->size switch at :123-152.
findings.toolingEvidence: mesh_rw.py:308-317 pack_normal writes a single u32; docs/BIG_MESH_GEOMETRY.md:127 documents 'Packed normal = one dword (type 4/0xc/0xd)'.
findings.discrepancy: match (no CPU decode exists; the relevant contract is the declaration typeCode)

findings.claim: For the normal element the engine selects internal typeCode 0xc (packed dword) exactly when InitFlags bit2 (&4) is set, keyed ONLY on &4 and NOT on &0x10 (unlike position, which also checks &0x10). The Banjo build uses layout='float' => InitFlags 0x14, so &4 is set => engine reads a PACKED normal (type 0xc), and the tooling correctly writes a packed normal for the same flags.
findings.engineEvidence: decomp_mesh_geo8.c CVertexShaderInputAnimated::Initialise :109-131: uVar1=param_1&4; normal element idx3 at :126-131 = (uVar1==0)?2(FLOAT3):0xc(packed) — depends only on &4. Position idx0 at :110-115 = ((&4==0)||(&0x10!=0))?2:0xd, so 0x14 gives FLOAT3 position but STILL a packed normal. Static Initialise :59-73 mirrors this (normal idx uses 0xc when &4).
findings.toolingEvidence: fable_core.py:458/:718 is_norm_comp=(init&4)!=0 (True for 0x14 -> 4-byte packed normal), and _calc_stride:456-467 gives 28 for skinned 0x14; compose_mesh (mesh_rw.py:735-737) sets stride=28, and :788 writes pack_normal() dword after the 12B FLOAT3 pos + 8B joints/weights, i.e. at normOff=20, matching docs §7.1 normOff=iOff+8.
findings.discrepancy: match

findings.claim: The exact bit layout the tooling emits (signed 11/11/10, ix=round(x*1023), iy=round(y*1023), iz=round(z*511), masks 0x7FF/0x7FF/0x3FF, little-endian) is byte-identical to EgoCore's PackNormal, whose meshes the retail engine loads correctly, and is exactly inverted by EgoCore/tooling UnpackNormal. This is the DEC3N (D3DDECLTYPE 14) convention that internal typeCode 0xc resolves to.
findings.engineEvidence: typeCode 0xc is in the 4-byte class (decomp_mesh_geo10.c:123-132 case 0xc -> sVar9=4), consistent with a single signed-10:11:11-in-a-dword D3DDECLTYPE. The concrete DAT_0129e9cc[0xc] byte is not dumped in the decomp outputs, so the literal D3DDECLTYPE enum value is not directly shown — inferred as DEC3N from the 4-byte size + the EgoCore constants that produce engine-loadable meshes.
findings.toolingEvidence: mesh_rw.py:308-317 pack_normal == EgoCore GltfMeshImporter.h:156-173 PackNormal (x*1023,y*1023,z*511, &0x7FF/&0x7FF/&0x3FF, ix|iy<<11|iz<<22); tooling/EgoCore decode fable_core decode_to_compose_args mesh_rw.py:950-960 and EgoCore GltfExporter.h:121-123 invert it identically.
findings.discrepancy: match

meshFindings.fix: No fix needed for normal-packing — it is not the deform bug. The tooling's pack_normal is byte-identical to EgoCore's proven PackNormal, is_norm_comp/stride/offset all agree with the engine's declaration for InitFlags 0x14 (skinned stride 28, normal dword at offset 20), and the engine selects a packed normal (type 0xc) precisely for the flags the build emits. The static flat-shading symptom, if real, is not caused by a wrong packed-normal bit layout; more likely candidates are (a) the normals fed in (smooth-vs-flat / wrong space) or (b) that DEC3N normalization (÷1023,÷511 then renormalize) makes near-axis normals slightly off but never 'flat' — so flat shading points at the material/lighting or the source normals, not the packing. The remaining unverified link is the literal DAT_0129e9cc[0xc] -> D3DDECLTYPE byte (not dumped in the decomp); to close it fully, dump 4 bytes at 0x0129e9cc+0xc*4 from the retail Fable.exe and confirm it equals D3DDECLTYPE_DEC3N (14). This suspect should be treated as ruled-out and effort redirected to the bone-slot mapping / inverse-bind path.

meshFindings.fix: No fix required for correctness of the weight/index byte format itself — it matches the documented engine layout. Two low-risk improvements: (1) Raise the influence cap from 3 to 4 in fable_core._resolve_skin (mesh_rw.py:503, `[:3]`) and _skin_bytes (mesh_rw.py:586, `infl[:3]`) and set BonesPerVertex=4 in compose_mesh (mesh_rw.py:761, `struct.pack('<IHB', b['vert_count'], 3, 1)`), so the 4th influence authored/normalized by build_banjo_animated.py (MAX_INFL=4) is not silently discarded — the engine reads a UBYTE4 (4 joint + 4 weight bytes) regardless. meshFindings.fix: No fix to the slot-mapping code is warranted from the evidence: the name->local-slot->palette-index chain in _resolve_skin/encode is correct against the documented engine model and round-trips through the RECOMPOSE oracle. To CONFIRM or rule this suspect out you must decompile the two engine functions that are ABSENT from hero_mesh_decomp.txt: (1) C3DMeshContent::Parse where it reads `u16 BoneIndices[2*BoneCount]` and each CAnimatedBlock's `u8 Groups[groupCount]`, and (2) the CVertexBufferWin32 draw-time skin path that builds the bone-matrix palette uploaded to the vertex shader. The decisive question: is the matrix palette indexed by LOCAL slot (Groups[] values used directly, as the tooling assumes) or is BoneIndices[] (local->global) applied first? If the latter, every skinned vertex is deformed by the WRONG bone and the fix is to remap in mesh_rw: joint byte should encode paletteIndex whose Groups[] entry is the GLOBAL id (via skel indices_raw), not the local slot. Separately, a real (non-slot) risk in build_banjo_animated.py:189-193 is disabling use_deform on many bones (fingers/toes/face/WEAPON_FOCUS/WEAPON_SCABBARD) BEFORE bone-heat: WEAPON_FOCUS being off means no Banjo vertices weight to it, which directly explains 'sword doesn't track hand' if the sword is a separate attached mesh expecting that bone to deform — but that is attachment/deform-enable, not slot mapping.

meshFindings.suspect: invbind-replaceable: engine inverse-bind/rest-pose handling (CalcLocalBoneTransformationRelative) + what ReplaceMeshByIndex validates of a swapped mesh

findings.claim: ReplaceMeshByIndex performs NO validation of a swapped mesh: it does not check vertex count, bone count, or skeleton match. It copies a fixed 14-byte graphic-info record (param_1*0xe stride into the def table at *(this+0x1c)+0x28) into graphic offsets 0x44..0x50 (3 dwords + 1 word = mesh handle/def ptr + type byte) and calls CreatePPhysicsMeshInfo. The only 'expectation' is the mesh TYPE byte: CreatePPhysicsMeshInfo dispatches on graphic[0xd]==5 (skinned) / ==4, else returns. So the engine accepts the Banjo swap unconditionally as long as the entry is type-5 — which the build emits.
findings.engineEvidence: ReplaceMeshByIndex @007a69f0 (decomp lines 12-48): 'pCVar2 = param_1*0xe + *(int*)(*(int*)(this+0x1c)+0x28)' then copies *(pCVar2) / +4 / +8 / +0xc (14 bytes) to iVar1+0x44..0x50; no count comparisons anywhere. CreatePPhysicsMeshInfo @007a... (lines 1624-1656): 'if (param_1[0xd]==5)...else if (param_1[0xd]!=4) return;' — pure type dispatch, still no count/skeleton check.
findings.toolingEvidence: build_banjo_animated.py:298-299 composes type-5; :367-373 big_write.rebuild edits MESH_HERO in place; staged gate :383 asserts ve['type']==5 and vs['count']==77. Composed mesh is a valid type-5 entry, so ReplaceMeshByIndex's only expectation (type byte) is satisfied.
findings.discrepancy: match — engine expects only a type-5 entry; tooling emits exactly that. 'Engine validates vertex/bone/skeleton and rejects/scrambles on mismatch' is NOT supported by the decomp.

findings.claim: The engine's inverse-bind / rest-pose consumer visible in this decomp is CalcLocalBoneTransformationRelative, which reads the mesh's BLOCK-4 TRS array (C3DMesh2 offset 0xa0, stride 0x30 = 48 bytes) as the per-bone ANIMATION BASE pose, copies it into the keyframe, then multiplies in the animation-delta quaternion (CQuaternion::operator*=) and ADDS the animation translation. Block-4 (48-B TRS) — not block-5 (64-B IBM) — is the rest/base pose the animation is layered onto. The tooling clones block-4 byte-exact from the hero, so the animation base pose for Banjo is IDENTICAL to the retail hero's.
findings.engineEvidence: CalcLocalBoneTransformationRelative @00a4d920 line 424: 'puVar13 = (undefined4*)(*(int*)(param_4+0xa0) + param_2*0x30)' copies 0x30 bytes as base keyframe; line 431 'CQuaternion::operator*=(param_1,&local_30)'; lines 432-434 add local_20/1c/18 to param_1+0x10/14/18. CalcLocalTransformationsRelative @00a4d770 line 233 confirms same 0xa0 base, 0x30 stride. operator*= @ line 2220 is a plain quaternion multiply.
findings.toolingEvidence: mesh_rw.clone_skeleton (mesh_rw.py:449) reads keyframes_raw = 48*bone_count bytes; _write_skeleton (:470,475) asserts len==48*n and re-emits byte-exact. build_banjo_animated.py:292-298 passes skeleton=skel (the hero's cloned blocks) unchanged. BIG_MESH_GEOMETRY.md:215 documents block-4 as the 48-B TRS 'BoneKeyframesRaw', bind pose ~identity quat + (-IBM translation).
findings.discrepancy: match — the animation base pose (block-4) and IBMs (block-5) are cloned byte-exact from the same hero rig the animations were authored for, so bind/rest space is not corrupted by the tooling.

findings.claim: The tooling's bind-space handling is internally self-consistent: the addon builds the rest armature from inverse(IBM) (block-5), places bones at model-space bind translations, and the build fits+weights Banjo into THAT rest pose; compose writes vertex positions VERBATIM with no axis/space transform. So decode->compose round-trips and a re-composed hero would deform correctly; Banjo verts live in the same native model frame the engine skins in.
findings.engineEvidence: Vertex-IBM application (CalcMeshTransformations / palette-matrix build that would multiply AnimBoneGlobal * IBM * vertex) is NOT present in this decomp — only the CalcLocal* animation-base functions are. The space the engine expects vertices in cannot be directly observed here.
findings.toolingEvidence: fable_core._decode_bones (fable_core.py:599-608): raw[12:16]=[0,0,0,1]; world=_invert4(IBM); head=world translation; matrix=world. import_op.py:114-131 sets eb.matrix=full bind matrix. mesh_rw.compose_mesh writes positions verbatim: struct.pack_into('<3f',out,o,pos[0],pos[1],pos[2]) (mesh_rw.py:206) — no transform. build_banjo_animated.py:79-86,147-164 fits Banjo to arm bone HEADS then bone-heat weights in rest pose.
findings.discrepancy: inconclusive for the final deform-space: the engine's vertex-side IBM multiply is absent from the decomp, so 'Banjo verts are in exactly the space the engine's skinning expects' cannot be positively confirmed from THIS decomp. The block formats and tooling round-trip are correct, but the fit uses only bone-HEAD positions (ignores bind ORIENTATION) and a single uniform scale — an authoring-quality risk, not an invbind FORMAT mismatch.

meshFindings.fix: No fix in the invbind/format layer: blocks 3/4/5 are cloned byte-exact and the engine (ReplaceMeshByIndex/CreatePPhysicsMeshInfo) imposes no count/skeleton validation, and CalcLocalBoneTransformationRelative's base pose (block-4 @0xa0) is identical to the retail hero's. This suspect does not explain the scramble via a bind-matrix or validation mismatch. If deform is still wrong, the residual risk this suspect surfaces is AUTHORING-space, not format: the Banjo fit (build_banjo_animated.py:147-164) matches only bone HEAD positions with one uniform scale and ignores each bone's bind ORIENTATION, so Banjo geometry sitting in the correct model frame can still be weighted such that animated rotation about a bone whose bind orientation differs from Banjo's local geometry twists wrongly. To confirm/deny definitively, obtain the missing engine vertex-skinning path (CalcMeshTransformations / the palette matrix = AnimBoneGlobal * IBM multiply) and verify the vertex-space convention; then hand the primary suspects (a) Blender vtx-group-name -> Fable bone-SLOT mapping and (c) packed joint/weight byte format, which govern WHICH bone drives each vertex and are the more likely scramble sources.

cardFindings.suspect: def-field-schema (CQuestCardDef field enumeration + what forge questcard.cpp writes)
cardFindings.fix: No schema fix needed. The def-field schema forge uses is correct and complete; the display-driving fields survive the clone. If pursuing the blank-values bug, the schema suspect should be dropped in favor of the runtime-population suspect: on the ACTIVE quest-start / held-card display path, objective text and gold/renown come from the runtime CTCQuestCard component (offsets +0x1c / +0x2c), written ONLY by the script setters SetQuestCardObjective (decomp l.150) and SetQuestCardGoldReward (decomp l.197), which locate the card by QUEST NAME via GetActiveQuestCardFromScriptName (decomp l.4688). A card that is displayed but was never populated by those per-quest setters (or whose donor def fields are themselves 0, or that was overwritten in-place with a zeroed def) shows blank regardless of the static def clone. The def only feeds the Logbook-draw-time fallbacks (GetQuestName=def+0x30, GetQuestSummary=def+0x2c, IsCore=def+0x58, GetRegionName fallback). Recommend the caller run the working recipe order (AddQuestRegion -> AddQuestCard -> SetQuestCardObjective/Gold/Renown -> GiveQuestCardDirectly) rather than editing the def.

meshFix.rootCause: The hero-mesh deform bug is NOT a byte-format mismatch. All three format-layer suspects (packed-normal bit layout, joint/weight byte encoding, inverse-bind/rest-pose blocks) are correctly ruled out: they are byte-identical to EgoCore's proven meshes, round-trip through the recompose oracle, and satisfy the only thing the engine actually validates on a swap (a type-5 entry, per ReplaceMeshByIndex @007a69f0 + CreatePPhysicsMeshInfo dispatching solely on graphic[0xd]==5). The single most-likely root cause is an AUTHORING-SPACE weighting error introduced in build_banjo_animated.py: the Banjo geometry is fit into the hero rig using ONLY bone HEAD positions and one global uniform scale (lines 79-151, `bhead = arm.matrix_world @ b.head_local`; `scale = body_h/bheight`; `fitted = ...`), and bone-heat weights it in that rest pose — bind ORIENTATION and per-bone scale are never consulted. Vertices therefore end up weighted to bones whose bind-frame axes do not match Banjo's local geometry, so any animated rotation about those bones twists/collapses the mesh even though the file round-trips perfectly. Compounding this, build_banjo_animated.py:184-193 explicitly clears use_deform on WEAPON_FOCUS, WEAPON_SCABBARD, all fingers/toes/face bones BEFORE bone-heat, so no Banjo vertices weight to WEAPON_FOCUS — which is the direct, mechanical explanation for 'sword doesn't track the hand' (the attached weapon expects deform on a bone that carries zero Banjo weight). The often-cited local-slot-vs-global-BoneIndices palette question is a real engine unknown but CANNOT be the cause here, because the build clones the donor hero's skeleton byte-exact (build_banjo_animated.py:292 `skel` from decode, passed unchanged at :298; indices_raw re-emitted verbatim at mesh_rw.py:446/472), so the local->global map is identical to the retail hero regardless of which convention the engine uses.

cardFix.rootCause: The empty OBJECTIVE and GOLD/RENOWN lines on the quest card are NOT a forge/def-schema defect — they are a runtime-population gap. The engine sources those three fields from the RUNTIME per-quest card THING (CTCQuestCard component: objective at +0x1c, gold at +0x2c) plus the manager's runtime quest list (DAT_013b89fc+0x6c), which are written ONLY by the script setters SetQuestCardObjective / SetQuestCardGoldReward / SetQuestCardRenownReward. Those setters first call GetActiveQuestCardFromScriptName (decomp l.4658-4701), which resolves a card only if an ACTIVE card THING exists for that quest script name (matched via card+0x28 CBasicString::Compare). forge (questcard.cpp author()) emits only the static CQuestCardDef + OBJECT clone and no companion quest script, so at display time no active card is populated and the branch in ConstructQuestList (param_3==1, l.1565-1710) that iterates the runtime list produces blank objective/reward. By contrast, TITLE and SUMMARY DO come from the static def via the card thing (GetQuestName reads def+0x30, GetQuestSummary reads def+0x2c), so forge's QuestName/QuestSummary fields are load-bearing and will render — UNLESS the caller passes a zero/out-of-range TextID, in which case GetPGroupEntry misses and the engine returns the empty default string DAT_013bca24, making title/summary ALSO blank. This second path is the one concrete thing forge can get wrong today: main.cpp asI32 (l.3814-3816) writes --quest-name/--quest-summary verbatim with no zero-guard and no symbol resolver, so `--quest-name 0` silently bakes a blank title. Net: objective/gold/renown emptiness = expected from a def-only card (fix is pipeline/scripting, not code); title/summary emptiness (if seen) = a bad/zero TextID that forge should reject.
